title: Density of primitive Pythagorean triples with hypotenuse ≤ N ~ N/(2π)

problemStatement.formal: Tendsto (fun N : ℕ => (primitiveTripleCount N : ℝ) / (N : ℝ)) atTop (𝓝 (1 / (2 * π)))
problemStatement.plain: The number of primitive Pythagorean triples (a,b,c) with hypotenuse c ≤ N is asymptotically N/(2π). The proof decomposes into three density factors: sector lattice points (π/8), coprime density (6/π²), and parity sieving (2/3).
whyMatters: Classical result in analytic number theory connecting geometry (circle), arithmetic (coprimality), and analysis (asymptotics)
Demonstrates the telescoping technique for density decomposition in formal mathematics

proven: Main density theorem proved from 3 axioms (primitiveTripleCount_density)
Partition identity: coprime sector = primitive + both-odd (coprime_sector_partition)
Parity axiom reduced: bothOdd/coprime → 1/3 implies parity axiom (parity_axiom_equivalent)
open: Sector lattice point density: sectorPointCount(N)/N → π/8 (Gauss circle problem)

insights: The coprime sector decomposes into exactly 2 parity classes (not 3): primitive (mixed parity) and both-odd. Both-even is impossible for coprime pairs.
The parity axiom (2/3 limit) is equivalent to bothOddCoprime/coprime → 1/3, a cleaner formulation involving a single residue class
Computational evidence shows the parity fraction oscillates around 2/3 for small N but stabilizes quickly

The three axioms have very different tractability: parity (combinatorial, possibly provable) >> coprime density (Möbius, very hard) > sector lattice points (Gauss circle, essentially impossible without analytic NT)
All main theorems are already proved from the 3 axioms - the file has 0 sorries

PythagoreanTriplesOQ01.lean has pre-existing Mathlib v4.26.0 API breakage: native_decide for bothOddCoprimeCount 100 and coprimeInSectorCount 100 return false values; parity_axiom_equivalent proof broken (sub_div rewrite pattern not found, Tendsto.const_sub signature changed). File needs API repair before new research.

The parity involution (m,n)→(m,m-n) gives an exact bijection OE↔OO in the coprime triangle. This proves |OE(K)|=|OO(K)| for all K, establishing the three-way partition is equitable in the triangle region.
column_discrepancy_bound axiom was FALSE: m=21, N=541 gives |sectorOE-sectorOO|=2, not ≤1. The bound fails because boundary coprime truncation can create imbalance >1 (120 violations found for m<50).

All 3 remaining axioms represent genuine analytic NT: Gauss circle problem (sector lattice density), coprime density in regions (Möbius sieving), parity equidistribution (CRT independence). Each requires ~500+ lines of formal infrastructure to eliminate.

The boundary analysis infrastructure (sector_boundary_balance, sector_oe_oo_discrepancy_bound) reduces the parity axiom to bounding O(√N) boundary effects, but formalizing this requires coprime count lower bounds which circularly depend on the sector axiom.
Aristotle companion file yielded 12 routine lemmas but cannot help with the deep axioms (these are open conjectures relative to Aristotle capabilities).
